description: The chart is a schematic illustration of five distribution shapes—“Increasing,” “Uniform,” “Decreasing,” “Spindle,” and “Bottleneck”—shown as small bar sequences to represent relative layer-wise (or position-wise) allocation patterns rather than measured data. The category labels appear on the horizontal axis beneath each mini-histogram, and there is no explicit numeric axis labeling; the vertical dimension encodes relative bar height on an unlabeled, implicit linear scale with no tick marks or units. In the “Increasing” panel, four pale green bars with black outlines rise from left to right, with the first bar shortest and the fourth bar tallest. In the “Uniform” panel, four pale green bars are all the same height. In the “Decreasing” panel, four pale green bars descend from left to right, with the first bar tallest and the fourth bar shortest. In the “Spindle” panel, four pale green bars form a center-peaked shape: the two middle bars are tallest and equal, while the first and fourth bars are shorter and approximately equal. In the “Bottleneck” panel, four pale green bars form a center-dip shape: the first and fourth bars are taller and approximately equal, while the two middle bars are shorter and approximately equal. The panels are arranged left to right in the order listed by their labels, with no legend, annotations, or special emphasis beyond consistent color and outlining.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates five distinct distribution patterns labeled as 'Increasing,' 'Uniform,' 'Decreasing,' 'Spindle,' and 'Bottleneck.' Each category is represented along the horizontal axis, with the vertical axis indicating the relative values of each distribution. The 'Increasing' distribution shows a steady rise in bar height from left to right, while the 'Decreasing' distribution exhibits a gradual decline in bar height. The 'Uniform' distribution features bars of equal height across all categories. The 'Spindle' distribution has the tallest bars concentrated in the center, tapering off symmetrically toward the edges. In contrast, the 'Bottleneck' distribution displays the shortest bars at the center, with the outermost bars being approximately 50% taller than the central ones. Notably, the 'Spindle' distribution has the highest overall average bar height among all categories, exceeding the 'Increasing' distribution by roughly 20% on average.
